title: Gabber lifting of quasi-excellence through an adic quotient
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $J\subseteq R$ an ideal. Suppose the canonical map $R\longrightarrow\varprojlim_{n\geq1}R/J^n$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. If $R/J$ is quasi-excellent [def-exc-excellent-ring], then $R$ is quasi-excellent. No assumption on the characteristic, universal catenarity or dimension is imposed.

source.place: Exposé I, Théorème 9.2 (Gabber), printed p.17, PDF p.23; arbitrary characteristic.

proof.text: Assume $R/J$ is quasi-excellent and suppose for contradiction that $R$ is not. Apply [lem-per-gabber-normal-counterexample-reduction] to the actual Noetherian complete pair $(R,J)$. Obtain a new domain $A$ and a nonzero nonunit $x\in A$: $A$ is normal, Nagata, universally catenary, $(x)$-adically complete and not quasi-excellent, but every quotient by a nonzero ideal is quasi-excellent. Its finite normalizations have all the additional properties in that node. This reduction imposes no characteristic restriction; in particular we do not apply the older rational-algebra version.

source.place: Kurano–Shimomoto, Ideal-adic completion of quasi-excellent rings (after Gabber), Theorem 5.1, Step 1; read online, local bibliographic copy WANTED in report.md.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-gabber-minimal-formal-defect] to this $A,x$. Choose a triple $(L,\mathfrak n,\mathfrak s)$ attaining its least height $h\geq2$. Write $B=B_L$ and $C=C_{L,\mathfrak n}$. Thus $\mathfrak s$ is a minimal singular prime of $C$ and $\mathfrak s\cap B=0$. Every $B_{\mathfrak q}$ of height at most $h$ is excellent. By [lem-per-gabber-semilocal-defect-height], for every finite $\gamma\subset\operatorname{Max}B$ containing $\mathfrak n$, the ring $D_\gamma$ and contracted prime $\mathfrak s_\gamma$ have the stated comparisons, $\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak s_\gamma=h>0$, and every member of $\Delta_\gamma(x)$ has height $h+1$ in $B$. Use exactly the normalized definition of $\Delta_\gamma(x)$ from these lemmas; its alternative description supplies a prime minimal over $\mathfrak s_\gamma+xD_\gamma$.

source.place: Kurano–Shimomoto, Ideal-adic completion of quasi-excellent rings (after Gabber), Theorem 5.1, Step 2 and Claim 5.4; read online, local bibliographic copy WANTED in report.md.

proof.text: For each prime $\mathfrak q\subset B$ of height at most $h$, apply [lem-per-qe-alteration-regular-neighbourhood] with $J=xB$: $B$ is a Noetherian domain, $B_{\mathfrak q}$ is excellent by Step 2, and $B/xB$ is quasi-excellent by the reduction. Obtain $b_{\mathfrak q}\notin\mathfrak q$, schemes $X_{\mathfrak q,i}$ regular above $V(x)$, and a proper surjective witness $V_{\mathfrak q}$ with an open cover mapping to them. Put $\Omega=\bigcup_{\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak q\leq h}D(b_{\mathfrak q})\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}B$. It is open and contains every prime of height at most $h$.

source.place: Kurano–Shimomoto, Ideal-adic completion of quasi-excellent rings (after Gabber), Theorem 5.1, Step 3, (5.12)–(5.13); read online, local bibliographic copy WANTED in report.md.

proof.text: We show $\Delta(x)\cap\Omega=\varnothing$. Suppose $Q$ lies in the intersection. By [lem-per-gabber-semilocal-defect-height], choose $\gamma$ and $\widetilde Q\supset\mathfrak s_\gamma+xD_\gamma$ contracting to $Q$. Choose $\mathfrak q$ with $Q\in D(b_{\mathfrak q})$. Both $\mathfrak s_\gamma$ and $\widetilde Q$ then lie in $\operatorname{Spec}D_\gamma[1/b_{\mathfrak q}]$: the former contracts to zero, and the latter contracts to $Q$. Base change the witness $V_{\mathfrak q}$ and its cover along $\operatorname{Spec}D_\gamma[1/b_{\mathfrak q}]\to D(b_{\mathfrak q})$. The new witness $V'$ is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change] and closed by the universal closedness in [def-weil-proper-morphism].

source.place: Kurano–Shimomoto, Ideal-adic completion of quasi-excellent rings (after Gabber), Theorem 5.1, Step 3, final diagram, printed pp.13–14; read online, local bibliographic copy WANTED in report.md.

proof.text: Lift $\mathfrak s_\gamma$ to a point $\xi_2$ of $V'$, using that surjectivity. Since $\mathfrak s_\gamma\subseteq\widetilde Q$, apply [lem-trf-closed-map-specializing] to the closed map $V'\to\operatorname{Spec}D_\gamma[1/b_{\mathfrak q}]$: a specialization $\xi_1$ of $\xi_2$ lies above $\widetilde Q$. Choose a member $V_i'$ of the pulled-back open cover containing $\xi_1$. It also contains its generalization $\xi_2$. Their images $\eta_1,\eta_2$ in $X_i'=X_{\mathfrak q,i}\times_B D_\gamma$ satisfy $\eta_2\rightsquigarrow\eta_1$. Write $\zeta_1$ for the image of $\eta_1$ in $X_{\mathfrak q,i}$. Its image in $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is $Q$, which contains $x$, so its local ring is regular by the closed-fibre conclusion of [lem-per-qe-alteration-regular-neighbourhood].

source.place: Kurano–Shimomoto, Ideal-adic completion of quasi-excellent rings (after Gabber), Theorem 5.1, Step 3, printed p.14, specialization lifting; read online, local bibliographic copy WANTED in report.md.

proof.text: The map $B\to D_\gamma$ is flat by [lem-per-gabber-semilocal-defect-height]. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine] its affine scheme map is flat; base change and stalks [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change, def-weil-flat-morphism] make $\mathcal O_{X_{\mathfrak q,i},\zeta_1}\to\mathcal O_{X_i',\eta_1}$ flat local. Its closed fibre is $\kappa(\zeta_1)$: because $x\in Q$, the fibre algebra factors through $D_\gamma/xD_\gamma=B_\gamma/xB_\gamma$. Every element inverted in $B_\gamma$ avoids $Q$, since $Q$ is the contraction of a prime of $D_\gamma$; its image in $\kappa(\zeta_1)$ is therefore already invertible. Thus tensoring this localized quotient with $\kappa(\zeta_1)$ gives exactly that field, with no extra residue extension. A field is regular local (zero maximal ideal and dimension zero). The source local ring is regular by Step 5. All target chart rings are finite type over the Noetherian $D_\gamma$: tensoring an affine finite-type presentation leaves the same finite generators. They are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], and their local rings are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-regular-with-regular-fibre] makes the local ring at $\eta_1$ regular.

source.place: Kurano–Shimomoto, Ideal-adic completion of quasi-excellent rings (after Gabber), Theorem 5.1, Step 3, printed p.14, flat closed-fibre comparison; read online, local bibliographic copy WANTED in report.md.

proof.text: The point $\eta_2$ generalizes $\eta_1$, so [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization] makes $\mathcal O_{X_i',\eta_2}$ regular. The point $\mathfrak s_\gamma$ contracts to the generic point of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ by [lem-per-gabber-semilocal-defect-height]. Consequently the local homomorphism $(D_\gamma)_{\mathfrak s_\gamma}\to\mathcal O_{X_i',\eta_2}$ is a stalk map of the base change, over $\operatorname{Frac}B$, of the generic fibre $X_{\mathfrak q,i}\times_B\operatorname{Spec}\operatorname{Frac}B$. That generic fibre is flat over its field by [lem-pc-flat-field]. Base change preserves flatness [lem-weil-pbc-flat-morphism-base-change], and [def-weil-flat-morphism] gives flatness of the indicated local map. Its source is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian], since $D_\gamma$ is Noetherian, and its target is Noetherian as in Step 6. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-under-regular]: it makes $(D_\gamma)_{\mathfrak s_\gamma}$ regular, contradicting the singularity asserted by [lem-per-gabber-semilocal-defect-height]. We have proved $\Delta(x)\cap\Omega=\varnothing$.

source.place: Kurano–Shimomoto, Ideal-adic completion of quasi-excellent rings (after Gabber), Theorem 5.1, Step 3, last paragraph, printed p.14; read online, local bibliographic copy WANTED in report.md.

proof.text: Write the closed set $\Omega^c$ as $V(H)$. By [lem-sc-finite-minimal-primes-over-ideal], $H$ has finitely many minimal primes. Every prime in $V(H)$ has height at least $h+1$, since $\Omega$ contains the primes of height at most $h$. For a height-$(h+1)$ member $Q$ of $V(H)$, choose among the primes $P$ with $H\subseteq P\subseteq Q$ one of least height; such a height exists since these primes have finite height at most $h+1$. It is minimal over $H$. Now $Q$ must equal $P$: if $P\subsetneq Q$ were a minimal prime over $H$, a chain of length at least $h+1$ ending at $P$, followed by $P\subsetneq Q$, would force $\operatorname{ht}Q\geq h+2$. By [lem-per-gabber-semilocal-defect-height], every member of $\Delta(x)$ has height $h+1$, so Step 7 puts $\Delta(x)$ inside this finite set of minimal primes. Hence $\Delta(x)$ is finite.

source.place: Kurano–Shimomoto, Ideal-adic completion of quasi-excellent rings (after Gabber), Theorem 5.1, Step 3, printed p.13, finiteness of the boundary; read online, local bibliographic copy WANTED in report.md.

proof.text: Finally apply [lem-per-qe-rotthaus-finite-boundary] with this $B,x,\mathfrak n,\mathfrak s$. The ring $B$ is Noetherian Nagata and $(x)$-adically complete by [lem-per-gabber-normal-counterexample-reduction]; $\mathfrak s$ is a minimal singular prime of $C$ by [lem-per-gabber-minimal-formal-defect]; the contracted primes have positive height $h$ by [lem-per-gabber-semilocal-defect-height]; and Step 8 proves finiteness of the very same normalized $\Delta(x)$. The criterion gives $\mathfrak s\cap B\ne0$, contradicting the chosen triple. This contradiction discharges the supposition in Step 1. Hence the original $R$ is quasi-excellent, as required.

source.place: Kurano–Shimomoto, Ideal-adic completion of quasi-excellent rings (after Gabber), Theorem 5.1, Step 3, application of Theorem 5.3; read online, local bibliographic copy WANTED in report.md.

Pass flatness to the base-changed chart and the generic fibre. This is generic algebra/topology used by the completion proof; the perverse unit supplies no replacement.
Ascend regularity along the flat local map whose closed fibre is a field. This is generic algebra/topology used by the completion proof; the perverse unit supplies no replacement.
Check that the finite-type chart rings over D_gamma are Noetherian. This is generic algebra/topology used by the completion proof; the perverse unit supplies no replacement.
Check Noetherianity of every stalk and prime localization used in regular-local criteria. This is generic algebra/topology used by the completion proof; the perverse unit supplies no replacement.
Pass regularity from the special chart point to its generalization. This is generic algebra/topology used by the completion proof; the perverse unit supplies no replacement.
Descend regularity from the generic chart stalk to the chosen defect stalk. This is generic algebra/topology used by the completion proof; the perverse unit supplies no replacement.
The closed complement has finitely many generic points. This is generic algebra/topology used by the completion proof; the perverse unit supplies no replacement.
The generic chart is flat over the fraction field before base change. This is generic algebra/topology used by the completion proof; the perverse unit supplies no replacement.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q135-5d6ca2a7d (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery: the item, its 9 steps and the 3 new nodes. Item statement: it matches ILO I Théorème 9.2 (p.17, local PDF) exactly, with no characteristic, catenarity or dimension hypothesis. ILO's text says Gabber's proof replaces Hironaka by uniformization in the Nishimura–Nishimura argument; in the DAG that piece is qe-alteration-regular-neighbourhood, which is already free of characteristic. New nodes: gabber-normal-counterexample-reduction, gabber-minimal-formal-defect and gabber-semilocal-defect-height are the existing lem-per-qe-* nodes word for word, minus the ℚ hypothesis. They are needed because the item's R is arbitrary, so they are strict generalizations, not duplicates, and none restates the item. Truth without ℚ: the existing split proof of qe-normal-counterexample-reduction uses ℚ only in the remark 'still a ℚ-algebra', and every lemma it cites (Marot Nagata lifting, normal-completion lifting, Jacobson G-ring criterion, finite-surjective descent, finite-type stability, Ratliff 0AW6) has no characteristic hypothesis. Claims 5.2 and 5.4 of Kurano–Shimomoto use no resolution, and that paper's Theorem 5.1 has no characteristic hypothesis. I did not have the paper locally (the report marks it WANTED), so for the nodes' content I relied on the already-reviewed qe-* nodes. Steps: the hypotheses of the alteration lemma, the semilocal node and the Rotthaus criterion are each discharged. I checked the Step 6 closed fibre myself: x maps to 0, S_γ avoids Q, so the fibre is κ(ζ1). Step 7's generic-fibre flatness via pc-flat-field plus base change is correct, and the Step 8 minimal-prime/height argument is correct and elementary. Batch-5 finding: lem-trf-closed-map-specializing is the general-topology fact Stacks 0066(1), a Mathlib leaf; neither the trace-formula nor the Poincaré-duality assumption gives it and it is no step of either proof, so it is accepted. The declared tool_uses are all generic commutative algebra and are accepted. No SGA source is used. No changes.
